answer: Every new agent must pass a bonded inlet: it posts a refundable stake that stays locked for a full horizon of graded work, co-signed by a sponsor. If later analysis merges two identities under one operator, both stakes are slashed and the sponsor's standing collapses. Faking a thousand agents therefore costs a thousand locked stakes plus forfeiture risk, while an honest agent risks only its own deposit. A ferrous iron-bodied hardware token can anchor the sponsor's signature, making mass registration physically awkward as well.
